root_cause.text: In `espintcp_sendmsg()`, after attempting to flush a pending partial send via `espintcp_push_msgs()`, the function unconditionally reinitializes `ctx->partial` with `sk_msg_init()` even when the previous partial send is still in progress (`emsg->len > 0`), causing reuse of live state and potential out-of-bounds read.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds a check `if (emsg->len) { err = -ENOBUFS; goto unlock; }` immediately after `espintcp_push_msgs()` and before `sk_msg_init(&emsg->skmsg)`, preventing reinitialization when a previous partial send is still pending. The commit message explicitly states: "Do not rebuild the send message when ctx->partial is still in progress. If espintcp_push_msgs() returns with emsg->len still set, fail the new send instead of overwriting the live partial state."
